MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below. Applicants must possess either education, as described below, or have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. For vacancies below the full-performance level of the position, the basic requirement will be evaluated on a developmental basis. Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process. GG-07, GG-09, and GG-11 Basic Requirements: Undergraduate or Graduate Education: Degree in computer science, engineering, information science, information systems management, mathematics, operations research, statistics, or technology management or degree that provided a minimum of 24 semester hours in one or more of the fields identified above and required the development or adaptation of applications, systems or networks. OR Attention to Detail - experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. My work or the data that I produce is typically reviewed by my supervisor or another colleague. Customer Service - experience having brief contact with customers to provide information about available information technology products and services and providing customers with standard products or routine services to address information technology needs Oral Communication - experience informing my supervisor and other IT staff of the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of basic technical information to a non-technical audience Problem Solving - identifying or selecting from a number of alternatives to address routine information technology-related issues by gathering and applying information from standard sources that provide a limited number of solutions. AND For the GG-07 position, qualifying experience is defined as: Experience communicating with customers about available services and providing products or services to address needs. For the GG-09 position, qualifying experience is defined as: Experience assisting, troubleshooting, documenting customer inquiries, and providing technical advice and assistance to customers. For the GG-11 position, qualifying experience is defined as: Experience troubleshooting computer problems in a manner that minimizes interruptions. For the GG12, applicants must possess the experience described below: GG-12 Basic Requirements: Attention to Detail- experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been asked by others to review their work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards Customer Service - experience maintaining relationships with customers, assessing current information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products and services that are tailored to meet customer needs Oral Communication -briefing mid-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of technical information to a non-technical audience Problem Solving - identifying alternatives to address complex information technology-related issues by gathering and applying information from a variety of sources that provide a number of potential solutions AND Qualifying Experience: To qualify, your resume must describe at least one year of experience that demonstrates the competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Experience refers to any paid or unpaid experience, including volunteer work and Military service, that would be considered equivalent to work normally performed at the next lower grade level in the federal service. . For the GG-12 position, qualifying experience is defined as: Experience resolving customer problems with system integration, research, evaluation of configuration issues with applications and/or desktop configurations. Volunteer Experience: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Candidates must describe how they meet the qualifying experience and/or selective placement factor(s) within the body of their resume. All qualifications must be met within 30 days after the closing date of this announcement.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Computer Science series. https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=Group-Standards Basic Requirements: Bachelor's degree in computer science or bachelor's degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of the 30 semester hours must have included any combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus. All academic degrees and course work must be from accredited or pre-accredited institutions. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is professional computer engineering and computer sciences guidance in the development of new software applications/systems and modifications to existing software applications/systems. Ideal Candidate: At least 2 years of coding and unit test experience in software application development using Razor/Blazor, .NET, C#, T-SQL, JavaScript, CSS3, HTML5, and Web APIs. At least 2 years of experience in SQL Server database design/stored procedures, SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS), and Team Foundation Server (TFS)/Azure DevOps/Git. Experience working independently and within a software development team, with a demonstrated ability to communicate clearly and concisely (both written and verbal), interact with customers, quickly understand technical objectives, provide effective solutions, and troubleshoot and fix software bugs. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Application of the disciplines and science of analysis, design, development, implementation, test evaluation and maintenance of computer software and associated software products over the system software life cycle. Ability to organize, prioritize, analyze, interpret and evaluate technical data, complex requirements and prediction of results in the solution of theoretical or practical data processing problems. Extensive knowledge of complex data formats, systems architecture, data analysis and display concepts and automated computational processes and methodology to respond to customer requirements with versatility and sound judgment. Ability to recognize and analyze problems, conducts research, summarize results, and provide appropriate recommendations and solutions to management. Ability to plan and execute complex, multi faced projects and/or studies within established time, financial, and/or time constraints to resolve software engineering questions. Skill and ability to negotiate complex issues, and communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, complex technical issues, report and briefing for senior military and civilian officials throughout the government and in private industry. Ability to establish and maintain relationships with key individuals/ groups inside and outside immediate working unit using high degree of tact and diplomacy. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Resumes for federal government positions need more detailed work descriptions and accomplishments than a typical private sector resume. Please be sure to clearly describe the full scope of your work experiences in your resume. Basic Requirement: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process. Attention to Detail - experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been asked by others to review their work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. Customer Service - experience maintaining relationships with customers, assessing current information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products and services that are tailored to meet customer needs. Oral Communication - briefing mid-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of technical information to a non-technical audience. Problem Solving - identifying alternatives to address complex information technology-related issues by gathering and applying information from a variety of sources that provide a number of potential solutions. In addition to the Basic Competency Requirements listed above: One year of specialized experience equivalent in level of difficulty and responsibility to that of the next lower grade GS-11 in the federal service, which demonstrates the ability to perform the duties of the position, is required. Specialized experience is defined as: Experience developing, implementing, coding, testing, operating, and modifying software and automated systems, and conducting systems requirement reviews; applying IT principles and practices in the software development process; experience using Common Business Oriented Language (COBOL) programming language to code and maintain software solutions. Volunteer Experience: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. You may qualify for consideration if meeting time-in grade, specialized experience, education requirement, 90 days after competitive appointment requirement, and all other qualification requirements within 30 calendar days after the closing date of the announcement, unless otherwise indicated on the announcement.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: As the world's largest finance and accounting firm, the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) pays all Department of Defense (DoD) military and civilian personnel, retirees and annuitants, and major DoD contractors and vendors. We take great pride in serving the men and women who serve America, and invite goal-oriented people like you to challenge yourself while providing a service to our nation. This position is being filled under the Direct Hire Authority for Certain Personnel of the Department of Defense via delegated authority by the Office of the Secretary of Defense. Positions may be filled as permanent or term with a full-time or part-time work schedule. Pay will vary by geographic location. We reserve the right to close this announcement early or to extend, as appropriate, based upon the needs of the Agency. Qualified application packages may be referred to management at various points in the selection process depending on the number and timing of applications received. Selections may be made at any point during the announcement open period. Veteran's Preference: Veteran's preference does not apply under this Direct Hire Authority (DHA).
MajorDuties: Provides development, implementation, operation, maintenance, and modification of major finance and/or accounting automation information systems to meet user needs and systems requirements.
Analyzes functional and technical requirements of IT systems to determine avenues of development or modification necessary to meet mission objectives.
Participates in systems requirement reviews and coordinates with customer to clarify requirements. Prepares system change/programming specifications, and specifies programming instructions.
Identifies alternative approaches to the design of current or proposed systems. Identifies how system modifications or new systems or subsystems affect current systems.

Prepares and executes tests for system or subsystem software validation. Reviews test results for effectiveness in meeting specifications and takes necessary corrective actions based on testing results.

You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Developing budget documentation and reports that comply with fiscal law and organizational financial management requirements; 2) Analyzing financial data to develop accurate forecasts, tracking obligations and expenditures; 3) Conducting regular reviews of IT portfolios to assess performance, value, and risks associated with IT investments; AND 4) Utilizing Information Technology Systems to route and track IT procurement requests. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11). The specialized experience must include, or be supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the competencies, as defined: (1) Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: completing thorough and accurate work independently, even in the most difficult or stressful situations; occasionally reviewing work completed by others; (2) Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: resolving routine and non-routine problems, questions, or complaints; developing and maintaining strong, mutually supportive working relationships with customers; conducting evaluation of support to determine quality of services and customer satisfaction, and recommending procedural changes based on customer need or changes in policy and/or regulation; (3) Decision Making - Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. (4) Information Management - Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems. (5) Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations. (6) Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: convincingly conveying complex information to customers; presenting thoughts that are well-organized and demonstrating confidence in the facts and ideas; adjusting style when working with individuals with different levels of understanding; using various methods to explain and convey information; and (7) Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: solving complex or sensitive problems by developing and proposing strategic alternatives; identifying possible conflicts and shared benefits; helping team anticipate problems and identifying and evaluating potential sources of information; providing feedback and coaching to others to help solve problems; engaging appropriate stakeholders when developing solutions in order to understand and incorporate multiple perspectives and needs; evaluating the effectiveness of decisions and adjusting future decisions as appropriate. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. MajorDuties: Develop, maintain, and update IT project plans, milestones, schedules, resource requirements, and risk-mitigation actions for assigned IT initiatives.
Coordinate IT project activities with stakeholders to achieve approved scope, schedule, cost, performance, and mission requirements.
Prepare project-status reports, decision papers, and briefings identifying project progress, resource requirements, issues, risks, and recommended courses of action for leadership.
Conduct regular reviews of the IT portfolio to assess the performance, value, costs, risks, and alignment of current and proposed IT investments with mission priorities.
Maintain complete and accurate IT portfolio documentation and project data in the approved portfolio-management system, including investment status, performance, cost, schedule, and risk information.
Analyze IT investment requirements and provide recommendations that align proposed solutions with organizational priorities, enterprise architecture, and applicable DoD requirements.
Develop IT acquisition-package documentation, including performance work statements, statements of requirements, independent Government cost estimates, and market-research documentation.
Prepare, route, track, and coordinate IT procurement requests through the approved IT acquisition process to obtain required technical, funding, and compliance approvals.
Coordinate with technical personnel, resource-management personnel, contracting officials, and other stakeholders to resolve IT acquisition issues and support timely procurement actions.
Monitor contractor performance and IT deliverables; identify deficiencies, coordinate corrective actions, and document results for technical and contracting stakeholders.
Prepare and coordinate IT purchase requests to help the organization obtain the right hardware, software, and services.
Evaluate vendor proposals and recommend IT products or services based on mission requirements, technical compatibility, cybersecurity considerations, performance standards, cost, and risk.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: As the world's largest finance and accounting firm, the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) pays all Department of Defense (DoD) military and civilian personnel, retirees and annuitants, and major DoD contractors and vendors. We take great pride in serving the men and women who serve America, and invite goal-oriented people like you to challenge yourself while providing a service to our nation. This position is being filled under the Direct Hire Authority for Certain Personnel of the Department of Defense via delegated authority by the Office of the Secretary of Defense. Positions may be filled as permanent or term with a full-time or part-time work schedule. Pay will vary by geographic location. We reserve the right to close this announcement early or to extend, as appropriate, based upon the needs of the Agency. Qualified application packages may be referred to management at various points in the selection process depending on the number and timing of applications received. Selections may be made at any point during the announcement open period. Veteran's Preference: Veteran's preference does not apply under this Direct Hire Authority (DHA).
MajorDuties: Serve as a project leader or consultant involved with all phases of the life cycle of a major financial automated information system.

Provides technical guidance, assists in determining priorities, ensures adequacy of project plans; and the analysis, design, testing, debugging, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance of software and systems.

Uses in-depth analysis to identify the size and scope of problems or new approaches being investigated. Coordinates maintenance and support activities of a major financial automated information system.
Briefs management on strategies to be used to exploit and implement new developments and advanced techniques in the area of software design and maintenance.
Ensures provision of adequate technical support of the major finance and/or accounting automated information systems. Ensures proper oversight of configuration management control procedures.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: This position is being filled under the Direct Hire Authority for Certain Personnel of the Department of Defense via delegated authority by the Office of the Secretary of Defense. We reserve the right to close this announcement early or to extend, as appropriate, based upon the needs of the Agency. Qualified application packages may be referred to management at various points in the selection process depending on the number and timing of applications received. Selections may be made at any point during the announcement open period.. Human Resources will determine your qualifications for each entry grade level based on your interest and the additional following criteria. Resumes for federal government positions need more detailed work descriptions and accomplishments than a typical private sector resume. Please be sure to clearly describe this in your resume. Combinations of education and experience may also be sufficient. Basic Requirement: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. In addition to the Basic Competency Requirements listed above, one year of specialized experience equivalent in level of difficulty and responsibility to that of the next lower grade GS-11 in the federal service, which demonstrates the ability to perform the duties of the position, is required. Specialized experience is defined as: Installing, configuring, testing and/or maintaining IT applications in accordance with customer needs and requirements; developing and analyzing product plans, release schedules, and product validity before release; and identifying, researching, and implementing emerging technology that enhances intranet and extranet capabilities. Volunteer Experience: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. You may qualify for consideration if meeting time-in grade, specialized experience, education requirement, 90 days after competitive appointment requirement, and all other qualification requirements within 30 calendar days after the closing date of the announcement, unless otherwise indicated on the announcement.

MajorDuties: As an Information System Security Officer (ISSO), assists the Information System Security Managers (ISSMs) in meeting their duties and responsibilities.
Implements and enforces all DoD Information System (IS) and Platform Information Technology (PIT) system cybersecurity policies and procedures, as defined by cybersecurity-related documentation.

Ensures all users have the requisite security clearances and access authorization and are aware of their cybersecurity responsibilities for DoD IS and PIT systems under their purview before granting access to those systems.
Conducts fact-finding meetings with customers to identify web page/internet requirements.
Researches web technologies to identify and apply new technologies to business practices.
Uses programming language (e.g., HTML, Java Script) to develop code for web pages.
Tests, debugs, modifies and validates web information before releasing the product to the customer.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: All qualification and time-in-grade (if applicable) requirements must be met within 30 days of the closing date of this announcement. You must meet the minimum qualification requirements as stated in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Operating Manual, Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, http://www.opm.gov/qualifications/Standards/group-stds/gs-prof.asp. Basic Requirement: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. For vacancies below the full-performance level of the position, the basic requirement will be evaluated on a developmental basis. Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process. Attention to Detail- experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been asked by others to review their work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. Customer Service- experience maintaining relationships with customers, assessing current information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products and services that are tailored to meet customer needs. Oral Communication- briefing mid-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of technical information to a non-technical audience. Problem Solving- identifying alternatives to address complex information technology-related issues by gathering and applying information from a variety of sources that provide a number of potential solutions. In addition to meeting the basic requirement, you must have one year specialized experience. NH-03: You must have one year of specialized experience at the next lover broadband NH-02, equivalent to the GS-11 grade level or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience must demonstrate support for RMF program support for information systems, including: Supporting RMF lifecycle activities, including categorization, control selection, control implementation, assessment preparation, authorization package development, and continuous monitoring. Familiarity with FedRAMP authorization, continuous monitoring, cloud security control implementation, shared responsibility models, and secure configuration practices for federal cloud environments. Preparing, reviewing, and maintaining RMF artifacts, including System Security Plans, control implementation statements, Security Assessment Reports, POA&Ms, risk acceptance documentation, assessment artifacts, and continuous monitoring records. Analyzing vulnerability scan results, configuration compliance data, audit findings, system changes, and assessment results to identify risk, support remediation, validate closure evidence, and document compensating controls. Practical understanding of Zero Trust architecture initiatives across ICAM, device compliance, network segmentation, application security, data, protection, telemetry, and automation pillars. NH-04: One year of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-03, equivalent to the GS-13 grade level or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience must demonstrate leadership or advisory responsibility for RMF program execution for complex, high-visibility, or enterprise information systems, including: Preparing, reviewing, and approving organizational cybersecurity and RMF policies, directives, procedures, and instructions to ensure alignment with federal, DoD, and organizational security requirements. Leading RMF planning, authorization readiness, control implementation reviews, assessment coordination, continuous monitoring, POA&M governance, risk acceptance analysis, and development of risk recommendations for leadership. Reviewing and validating authorization packages, security control evidence, vulnerability remediation strategies, cloud security responsibilities, system interconnections, software assurance results, and major system changes to determine cybersecurity risk and mission impact. Advising system owners, program managers, technical teams, assessors, contractors, and leadership on RMF execution, documentation quality, control implementation, audit readiness, vulnerability prioritization, Zero Trust alignment, and secure system lifecycle requirements. Leading cross-functional coordination across acquisition, engineering, operations, security, and executive stakeholders to resolve cybersecurity risks, support authorization decisions, maintain continuous monitoring visibility, and align RMF activities with mission priorities. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. MajorDuties: NH03: This position serves as an Information System Security Officer (ISSO), supporting Risk Management Framework (RMF) execution for information systems through security control implementation and assessment, authorization package development, evidence collection, vulnerability tracking, Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) management, and continuous monitoring. Experienced in executing RMF activities for assigned information systems, applying cybersecurity principles, security controls, vulnerability management, continuous monitoring, and applicable federal, DoW, organizational, and Zero Trust requirements. Experienced in evaluating security control implementation and effectiveness; maintains authorization documentation; analyzes assessment evidence and findings; manages POA&Ms; and monitors security posture. Provides technical cybersecurity guidance and recommendations to system owners and stakeholders regarding security requirements, risks, controls, remediation, and authorization decisions. Experience in analyzing security documentation, vulnerability and configuration data, assessment findings, and system changes to identify security weaknesses, evaluate risk, and recommend remediation, mitigation, or compensation controls. Evaluates cybersecurity impacts of system changes and resolves or recommends solutions for complex issues involving vulnerabilities, control deficiencies, technical limitations, and competing mission and security requirements. Coordinates with technical stakeholders to validate remediation actions and security evidence and independently determines whether deficiencies have been adequately addressed. Evaluates cybersecurity practices and controls to identify gaps, risks, and improvement opportunities associated with Zero Trust, vulnerability management, continuous monitoring, and emerging cybersecurity requirements. Identifies recurring or systemic vulnerabilities and control weaknesses and recommends corrective actions or risk mitigation strategies. Develops technical analyses, risk assessments, metrics, reports, and briefings on system security posture, authorization status, vulnerabilities, remediation, and continuous monitoring results. NH04: This position serves as a senior ISSM and cybersecurity technical authority for a portfolio of complex, high-profile enterprise systems, programs, and modernization initiatives. Establishes technical priorities and governance for RMF execution, security controls, authorization readiness, continuous monitoring, vulnerability management, and POA&M oversight. Interprets and applies federal, DoW, organizational, and emerging cyber security requirements to resolve complex issues and ensure consistent risk management across the portfolio. Integrates cybers security risk information across systems and programs to identify significant or systemic weaknesses and mission impacts. Reviews and validates significant control deficiencies, remediation strategies, compensating controls, cloud security, system interconnections, software assurance, and major system changes. Develops risk-management strategies and recommendations for complex issues extending beyond the individual system level and advises leadership on authorization, operational, acquisition, and risk decisions. Advises senior leadership, system owners, program managers, and technical officials on cyber security risk, authorization readiness, vulnerability priorities, Zero Trust, cloud security, modernization, and emerging requirements. Leads integration of cyber security requirements and risk considerations across engineering, acquisition, operations, and program organizations to resolve significant cross-functional issues. Presents executive-level risk analyses, metrics, trends, and recommendations addressing portfolio security posture, systemic risks, and issues affecting mission execution. Certifications: Positions require a current cybersecurity certification appropriate to the role and grade level in alignment with DoD 8140 cyber workforce requirements, such as Security+, CySA+, CASP+, CISSP, CISM, or an equivalent ISSO/ISSM qualifying certification.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Current USACE Employees with Competitive Status Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technician Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD MR and NG Preference Eligible Tech Receiving Disability Retirement Priority Placement Program, DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience GS-13: One year of specialized experience which includes:1)Serving as a subject matter expert on cyber security threat intelligence or vulnerability management, performing activities to monitor emerging cyber threats, determine relevance to an organization or mission, assess level of exposure, and assist with the prioritization of response activities. 2) Analyzing security alerts, event log files, and collected evidence to identify network intrusion artifacts, and fusing computer network attack analyses with criminal and counterintelligence investigations and operations.3) Enhancing cyber security capabilities by evaluating security architectures, integrating security policy into IT systems, and managing the procurement and implementation of new security tools and systems in compliance with Department of Defense (DoD) and Army regulations.4) Developing and presenting technical briefings, presentations, and reports on IT security threats, vulnerabilities, and recommended mitigation actions to organizational leadership and external stakeholders. All experience areas shall additionally demonstrate each of the following competencies: 1) Attention to Detail, 2) Customer Service, 3) Oral Communication, and 4) Problem Solving. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-12). The specialized experience must include, or be supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the four competencies, as defined: (1) Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: completing thorough and accurate work independently, even in the most difficult or stressful situations; occasionally reviewing work completed by others. (2) Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: resolving routine and non-routine problems, questions, or complaints; developing and maintaining strong, mutually supportive working relationships with customers; conducting evaluation of support to determine quality of services and customer satisfaction, and recommending procedural changes based on customer need or changes in policy and/or regulation. (3) Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: convincingly conveying complex information to customers; presenting thoughts that are well-organized and demonstrating confidence in the facts and ideas; adjusting style when working with individuals with different levels of understanding; using various methods to explain and convey information. (4) Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: solving complex or sensitive problems by developing and proposing strategic alternatives; identifying possible conflicts and shared benefits; helping team anticipate problems and identifying and evaluating potential sources of information; providing feedback and coaching to others to help solve problems; engaging appropriate stakeholders when developing solutions in order to understand and incorporate multiple perspectives and needs; evaluating the effectiveness of decisions and adjusting future decisions as appropriate. Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-12).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position serves as an Information Technology Specialist (INFOSEC) for the US Army Corps of Engineers, acting as a subject matter expert on cyber security intelligence to enhance the organization's security posture. The role involves analyzing network threats, conducting counterintelligence and criminal investigations into computer intrusions, and implementing new security measures to protect IT systems.
Details.SubAgencyName: G-6 CYBER SECURITY DIRECTORATE CYBER NETWORK DEFENSE DIVISION
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Build Strong With Us at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), where engineering excellence meets public service. As the Nation's premier engineering, design, and construction management agency, we deliver innovative and efficient solutions that strengthen national security, support economic growth, and reduce disaster risks for communities across the country. At USACE, you will find meaningful work, collaborative teams, and opportunities to grow your career while making a lasting impact. We seek talented professionals with vision, creativity, leadership, and technical expertise to help solve some of the Nation's toughest engineering challenges. Build your purpose. Build your profession. Build your future. Discover why USACE is a great place to work and Build Strong With Us.
MajorDuties: Prepare and deliver technical presentations, engineering proposals, and after-action reports to inform leadership on the status of security projects.
Enhance cybersecurity capabilities by evaluating security architectures and managing the acquisition and implementation of new tools, systems, and software.
Fuse computer network attack analyses with criminal and counterintelligence investigations to support legal and operational actions.
Monitor external data sources to maintain an up-to-date understanding of cyber threat conditions and their potential impact on the enterprise.
Analyze computer-generated threats, log files, and collected evidence to identify the perpetrators of network intrusions.
Gather evidence on criminal or foreign intelligence entities to mitigate real-time threats and support the prosecution of computer crimes.

Basic Requirement: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process. Attention to Detail - experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been asked by others to review their work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. Customer Service - experience maintaining relationships with customers, assessing current information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products and services that are tailored to meet customer needs. Oral Communication - briefing mid-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of technical information to a non-technical audience. Problem Solving - identifying alternatives to address complex information technology-related issues by gathering and applying information from a variety of sources that provide a number of potential solutions. In addition to the Basic Competency Requirements listed above: One year of specialized experience equivalent in level of difficulty and responsibility to that of the next lower grade GS-12 in the federal service, which demonstrates the ability to perform the duties of the position, is required. Specialized experience is defined as: Evaluating, customizing, software and systems across the full software development life cycle (SDLC), including analysis, design, development, programming, testing, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance; establishing, configuring, and securing Application Programming Interface (API) connections, integrations, and web services such as REST, SOAP, GraphQL; conducting systems requirement reviews and implementing modifications. Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates to paid employment. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Resumes for federal government positions need more detailed work descriptions and accomplishments than a typical private sector resume. Please be sure to clearly describe the full scope of your work experiences in your resume. Basic Requirement: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process. Attention to Detail- experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been asked by others to review their work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. Customer Service- experience maintaining relationships with customers, assessing current information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products and services that are tailored to meet customer needs. Oral Communication- briefing mid-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of technical information to a non-technical audience. Problem Solving- identifying alternatives to address complex information technology-related issues by gathering and applying information from a variety of sources that provide a number of potential solutions. In addition to the Basic Competency Requirements listed above: One year of specialized experience equivalent in level of difficulty and responsibility to that of the next lower grade GS-11 in the federal service, which demonstrates the ability to perform the duties of the position, is required. Specialized experience is defined as: Experience developing, implementing, coding, testing, operating, and modifying software and automated systems, and conducting systems requirement reviews; applying IT principles and practices in the software development process. Volunteer Experience: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/competency-based-policy/general-schedule/2200/2210-competency-based-policy/competency-based-qualification-standard/ BASIC REQUIREMENT OR INDIVIDUAL OCCUPATIONAL REQUIREMENT: OPM: General Schedule Qualification Standard for Information Technology (IT) Management Series, 2210 (Alternative A)Experience must be IT related; the experience may be demonstrated by paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training (for example, IT certification), as appropriate GS-5 through GS-15 (or equivalent): For all positions individuals must have IT-related experience demonstrating each of the four competencies listed below. The employing agency is responsible for identifying the specific level of proficiency required for each competency at each grade level based on the requirements of the position being filled. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately . Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: AND SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02 or equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 in the Federal Service. Specialized experiences includes: Planning, coordinating, and installing applications software and hardware operation systems. Administering and maintaining assigned systems. Providing technical guidance and instructions to users and other IT specialists. Troubleshooting complex problems and providing support in a manner that minimizes interruptions in customer's work process. Maintaining liaison with manufacturers, professional organizations, and counterparts at other installations and services regarding technologies and advancements, and participating as a key senior member and advisor on special committees and special projects designed to study methods to enhance the use of information technology throughout installations. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of the principles, methods, and practices for integrating information system components sufficient to plan, coordinate, and administer computer systems, and optimize system performance. Knowledge of the latest advancements in technology to initiate corrective or preventative action to ensure optimum performance of the system. Knowledge of performance tuning tools, database management, and project management methods sufficient to optimize systems performance, troubleshoot database performance problems, and perform a wide range of systems administration functions. Knowledge of operating systems, associated devices, and the interoperability of systems sufficient to install, upgrade, troubleshoot, test, and maintain those systems; to optimize the functionality and performance of systems; and to ensure the availability, integrity, efficiency, and reliability of servers. Ability to apply methods and practices for troubleshooting, recovering, adjusting, modifying, and improving systems to solve complex problems, provide support that minimizes interruptions in service to customers, and maintain liaison with industry and other activities to provide awareness of state-of-the-art technology. Ability to communicate orally and in writing. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Basic Requirement: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: U.S. Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: Providing immediate response and resolution to information technology tickets. Analyzing information technology helpdesk tickets for escalation. Diagnosing hardware or software problems. Briefing senior leadership and providing status updates on projects and challenges. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11) The specialized experience must include, or be supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the four competencies, as defined: (1) Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: completing thorough and accurate work independently, even in the most difficult or stressful situations; occasionally reviewing work completed by others. (2) Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: resolving routine and non-routine problems, questions, or complaints; developing and maintaining strong, mutually supportive working relationships with customers; conducting evaluation of support to determine quality of services and customer satisfaction, and recommending procedural changes based on customer need or changes in policy and/or regulation. (3) Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: convincingly conveying complex information to customers; presenting thoughts that are well-organized and demonstrating confidence in the facts and ideas; adjusting style when working with individuals with different levels of understanding; using various methods to explain and convey information. (4) Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: solving complex or sensitive problems by developing and proposing strategic alternatives; identifying possible conflicts and shared benefits; helping team anticipate problems and identifying and evaluating potential sources of information; providing feedback and coaching to others to help solve problems; engaging appropriate stakeholders when developing solutions in order to understand and incorporate multiple perspectives and needs; evaluating the effectiveness of decisions and adjusting future decisions as appropriate

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: These positions are located within the Department of War Education Activity (DoDEA) Information Technology Division's Global Operations Branch at either Fort Bragg, North Carolina or Fort Campbell, Kentucky. This is a Direct Hire Solicitation.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA), as one of only two Federally-operated school systems, is responsible for planning, directing, coordinating, and managing prekindergarten through 12th grade educational programs on behalf of the Department of War (DoW). DoWEA is globally positioned, operating 160 accredited schools in 8 districts located in 11 foreign countries, 7 states, Guam, and Puerto Rico. DoWEA employs approximately 15,000 employees who serve more than 72,000 children of active duty military and DoW civilian families. DoWEA is committed to ensuring that all school-aged children of military families are provided a world-class education that prepares them for postsecondary education and/or career success and to be leading contributors in their communities as well as in our 21st century globalized society.
MajorDuties: Analyze incident request trends and patterns in order find opportunities to improve services.
Analyze, document, and plan for additions, upgrade, or configuration to ensure proper application software and web services.
Analyze hardware and software problems for on-the-spot repair/replacement or referral for other repairs.
Remove, reinstall or reconfigure desktop software or web services in order to correct issues.
Monitor helpdesk system for newly submitted tickets, documents, and update existing tickets until complete resolution.
Test new software deployment packages and Operating System images and provide feedback or solutions.

MajorDuties: Serves as senior Security Control Assessor leading assessments of information systems. Applies experience as network engineer, web administrator, developer, or DBA using Nessus, Fortify, or Burp Suite to evaluate security control effectiveness.

Plans, develops, and executes detailed security assessment plans for management, operational, and technical controls per RMF, NIST 800-53, and DoDI 8510.01. Performs hands-on technical testing across networks, web applications, databases, and cloud.

Identifies system weaknesses and vulnerabilities in complex IT environments through comprehensive testing using eMASS, Tenable Nessus, Fortify, and Burp Suite. Analyzes results to determine residual risk and control effectiveness.

Prepares comprehensive assessment reports, risk documentation, and authorization packages. Provides technically sound recommendations to leadership, SCA, Authorizing Officials, and senior leaders on system risk posture.

Serves as technical authority and mentor to junior assessors and IT staff. Provides expert guidance on secure system configuration, RMF processes, security tool usage, and mitigation strategies for complex enterprise systems.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: The experience described in your resume will be evaluated and screened from the Office of Personnel Management's (OPMs) basic qualifications requirements. See: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/competency-based-policy/general-schedule/2200/2210-competency-based-policy/competency-based-qualification-standard/ for OPM qualification standards, competencies and specialized experience needed to perform the duties of the position as described in the MAJOR DUTIES and QUALIFICATIONS sections of this announcement by 11/09/2026 Applicant must have directly applicable experience that demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies/knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have specialized experience sufficient to demonstrate that you have acquired all the competencies necessary to perform at a level equivalent in difficulty, responsibility, and complexity to the next lower grade GS/GG-12 in the Federal service and are prepared to take on greater responsibility. Generally, this would include one year or more of such specialized experience. Specialized experience for this position includes: Utilizing a wide range of Cybersecurity and advanced Information Technology concepts, principles, and practices to apply to difficult and complex work assignments; Identifying, documenting and communicating security plan vulnerabilities; Utilizing risk management principles to perform risk analysis; Evaluating and applying information assurance regulations, policies, and procedures to analyze operating/developmental computer systems and identifying deficiencies in their ability to safeguard classified data and information. Specifically you will be evaluated on the following competencies: 1. Cybersecurity - Support protection of the confidentiality, integrity, non-repudiation, and availability of systems, networks, and data through planning, analysis, development, penetration testing, access control, implementation, maintenance, and enhancement of information security systems, programs, policies, procedures, and tools. 2. Risk Management - Knowledge of the principles, methods, and tools used for risk assessment and mitigation, including assessment of failures and their consequences. 3. Problem Solving - Identifies and analyzes problems; weighs relevance and accuracy of information; seeks/generates and evaluates alternative perspectives/solutions; makes timely/ effective recommendations, based on potential implications of findings or conclusions. Critically evaluates to identify the causes of problems, and chooses courses of action that balance the interests of the mission and stakeholders. 4. Communications - Communicate (i.e., written and oral) rights, responsibilities, management directives, policies, and/or regulations to employees, supervisors, and/or other pertinent individuals.

Details.JobSummary: DCSA's Industrial Security Field is looking for Information Systems Security Professionals (ISSP) with responsibility for oversight of complex information assurance utilizing Risk Management Framework & cybersecurity related activities at cleared contractor sites across the country. The ISSP employs technical knowledge and interpersonal skills to ensure information systems security managers understand and implement the technical controls and processes required to protect classified information.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Our Mission Through vetting, industry engagement, education, and counterintelligence and insider threat support, secure the trustworthiness of the United States Government's workforce, the integrity of its cleared contractor support, and the uncompromised nature of its technologies, services, and supply chains. Our Vision DCSA's elite security experts illuminate national security risks to empower faster, smarter decision-making that protects American innovation and resilience to enable mission success. DCSA Strategic Execution Plan The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency stands at the intersection of government-wide trusted workforce, national security, and industrial base protection. Guided by the Secretary of War's National Defense Strategy, Deputy Secretary's Warfighting Acquisition Transformation efforts, and Trusted Workforce 2.0, our mission is to deliver data-driven, threat-informed, and customer-trusted security services at scale. The FY2026 - 2028 DCSA Strategic Execution Plan defines six strategic priorities for the agency: Deliver NBIS Deploy NI2 to Modernize Industrial Security Modernize and Sustain Trusted Workforce Determinations Rebuild the Workforce Compact Operate as a Customer-Centric Business Drive Audit-Ready Integration and Agency Efficiency with AI
MajorDuties: As an INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SPECIALIST (INFOSEC) you will be responsible for the following duties: -Serve as an Information Systems Security Professional (ISSP) within the assigned region. -Perform Cybersecurity activities including security control assessments of information systems to include assess and authorize activity utilizing the Risk Management Framework (RMF). -Exercise security oversight of cleared contractor information systems within the National Industrial Security Program (NISP). -Analyze, assess, evaluate, verify and validate cleared contractor information system security plans and security controls; and, make authorization risk recommendations to the Authorizing Official. -Document security assessments, advise/assist, etc. for Information Systems assigned -Engage and interface with industry security professionals to assess implemented security controls. -Evaluate security control requirements, recommend configurations for information systems and networks and identify strategies to manage risk through mitigation of vulnerabilities, considering the rapidly evolving Cybersecurity threat to information systems. -Serve as spokesperson at meetings to convey NISP and RMF implementation guidance and Cybersecurity information relating to industrial security.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below. For vacancies below the full-performance level of the position, the basic requirement will be evaluated on a developmental basis. Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process. Attention to Detail- experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been asked by others to review their work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Resumes for federal government positions need more detailed work descriptions and accomplishments than a typical private sector resume. Please be sure to clearly describe the full scope of your work experiences in your resume. Basic Requirement: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. In addition to the Basic Competency Requirements listed above, one year of specialized experience equivalent in level of difficulty and responsibility to that of the next lower grade GS-11 in the federal service, which demonstrates the ability to perform the duties of the position, is required. Specialized experience is defined as providing customer support and project reviews for information technology contingency planning initiatives; conducting technical Information Technology tasks and cybersecurity and technical assessments of planned and installed automated information systems; installing, configuring, troubleshooting, and maintaining customer hardware and software. Volunteer Experience: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. You may qualify for consideration if meeting time-in grade, specialized experience, education requirement, 90 days after competitive appointment requirement, and all other qualification requirements within 30 calendar days after the closing date of the announcement, unless otherwise indicated on the announcement. We may use this announcement to fill additional vacancies within 90 days of the closing date.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Computer Science series. https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=Group-Standards SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-12 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience that demonstrates designing, testing, and deploying telemetry data processing, data acquisition, and real-time visualization products supporting Test and Evaluation (T&E) missions. Planning and executing real-time mission room support, including monitoring and analyzing the integrity of real-time telemetry data streams. Troubleshooting and maintaining telemetry signal processing systems, test range sensors, and related hardware/software architectures. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. Ideal Candidate: The ideal candidate is an experienced computer engineer or computer scientist with a strong background in real-time telemetry, data processing, and test-support operations. The candidate can apply sound engineering judgment to solve complex hardware, software, and data-integration issues; develop reliable solutions under time-sensitive conditions; and improve tools, procedures, and data displays that support test missions. The ideal candidate also demonstrates technical leadership, attention to detail, commitment to security and mission readiness, and the ability to work effectively with customers and multidisciplinary engineering teams. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1.Ability to inspire, motivate, and guide others toward goal accomplishment. Leadership ability, including the ability to coach, mentor and challenge subordinates. Ability to adapt leadership style to a variety of situations and model high standards of honesty, integrity, trust, and respect for the individual by applying these values to daily behaviors. 2. Knowledge of state-of-the-art real-time and post-flight mission room systems and related hardware and software and its application to the support of weapon system test and evaluation. 3. Skill/ability to apply computer scientist/engineer procedures, requirements, regulations, and policies related to mission support systems especially in real-time processing systems, 4. Knowledge of highly sophisticated aircraft systems, telemetry, real-time data acquisition systems and state-of-the-art computer hardware/software. 5. Knowledge of test range instrumentation and sensors, how they are used, and how the resulting data is processed. 6. Ability to recognize and analyze problems, conduct research, summarize results, and make appropriate recommendations. 7. Ability to communicate both orally and in writing on technical issues, results, requirements, accomplishments, program status, and project financial status. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
